Aisha: Heads-up — Tenant 'GlowCo' go-live tomorrow 09:00 PST. Quick ops notes for caching/batching/streaming to keep latency under 300ms and de-risk renewals. See thread.

Marco: TL;DR: small shared cache (1–5s TTL) for warm prefixes, per-tenant warm pool of 2 workers, adaptive batching up to 8 tokens/req, limit batch window to 50ms.

Devon: Circuit-breaker: if p50 > 250ms for 2m, flip to stream-only + reduced batch size (2) and route to fallback model 'gpt-small-q4'. Also enable fast cooldown (30s) before trying to restore.

Lily: How will we surface renewal risk? Customer cares about SLAs and quality — want early warning if latency or hallucination spikes.

Aisha: Actionable runbook: 1) Health pulse every 15m → if throughput drops or latency up, page oncall; 2) Weekly usage + quality sync with customer; 3) Capture 5 golden prompts from their flows for automated evals; 4) Renewal flag: >3 incidents in 30d or NPS < 7 triggers AE outreach.

Marco: config snippet:
```yaml
inference:
  cache:
    shared_ttl_ms: 3000
    per_tenant_pool: 2
  batching:
    max_batch_size: 8
    max_wait_ms: 50
  fallback:
    model: gpt-small-q4
    batch_size: 2
    route_policy: latency_first
```

Devon: Observability checklist (add to tenant dashboard): p50 > 250ms (2m), p95 > 800ms (1m), error-rate > 1% (5m). Log sample windows: store 100 recent requests + 5 failed responses for quality review. Ticket template: impact, steps taken, next steps, customer notification.

cs-bot: Runbook doc updated: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tenant-burst-ops — added GlowCo specifics :sparkles: 

Lily: This looks great. Can you share a one-page customer-facing summary I can send to GlowCo?

Aisha: I'll draft a 1-pager with the health checklist + escalation contacts by EOD. I'll @Marco @Devon for the tech appendix.

Marco: Happy to provide appendix. Also: recommend enabling prefix caching for top-10 intents only, and a short TTL so we don't stale personalization.

Lily: Thanks team :pray:
